subject: Post-call: tenancy/SLAs & noisy-neighbor concerns — next steps
summary: After a product discovery call with TrueNorth Health, the customer requested clarification on isolation guarantees and SLOs between Hosted API, Dedicated capacity, and Private VPC. They are concerned about noisy-neighbor performance regressions for a clinical triage assistant and asked for a technical POC. Next steps: schedule POC with Solutions Eng (Monica) and Infra (Aditya), share isolation playbook and SLA comparison, confirm traffic patterns and retention/PII constraints.
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Lee <karen.lee@truenorthhealth.com>, Mark Davis <mark.davis@truenorthhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 20 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: tenancy/SLAs & noisy-neighbor concerns — next steps

Hi Karen / Mark —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap + proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- What we heard: primary concern is tail latency and predictable per-request SLOs for your clinical triage assistant (peak concurrent sessions ~150, median prompt length ~250 tokens, spikes up to ~600). You called out "noisy neighbor" interference on shared infra as a blocker for Hosted API unless we can guarantee isolation.
- Risk surface: latency tail, cold-starts for large-context sessions, and GPDR/PHI retention policies for conversations.
- Options we discussed: Hosted API (fast onboarding), Redwood Dedicated (reserved GPU pools + burst), and Private VPC (customer-managed networking, on-prem if required).

Proposed immediate next steps: 
1) Run a short technical POC focused on tail latency and isolation (we'll replay a small representative traffic profile).
2) Solutions Eng (Monica) + Infra lead (Aditya) to join POC call for configuration and kernel/quantization tuning.
3) We'll share our "isolation playbook" and a short SLA comparison doc to highlight differences in guarantees and operational controls.

Could you confirm: 
- A good time window for a 60–75 minute technical POC next week (we have availability Tue/Wed afternoon PT).
- A contact on your side for the infra/DevOps person who can open network access and run the sample workload (name + email).
- Any regulatory constraints (retention limits, encryption-at-rest/KMS requirements) beyond HIPAA baseline?

Attaching the proposed agenda for the POC in the follow-up (Monica will add the playbook).

Thanks — I want to make sure the POC answers the noisy-neighbor and SLO questions concretely.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra

Subject: Re: Post-call: tenancy/SLAs & noisy-neighbor concerns — next steps

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear recap. Wed 23 Jun 1:30pm PT works for us for the POC call. I'll confirm calendar invites after I check with Mark.

A few clarifications to help you scope the workload: 
- Typical steady-state: ~40 qps across 4 endpoints; spikes to 220 qps for 10–15 minutes during morning batch intake.
- Our acceptable SLO target: 99.9% of requests under 300ms server-side token latency for short prompts (<=150 tokens); longer context flows can be 700–900ms but tails are the issue.
- We cannot ship logs or raw PHI off-cluster to third-party storage without a Business Associate Addendum. For the POC we can use synthetically masked data but need to validate encryption in flight/rest and audit log retention.

For the infra contact, bring Mark (mark.davis@truenorthhealth.com) — he'll be on the POC call.

Also, are you able to share a short comparison of what you can SLAs on hosted vs dedicated vs private? We need an explicit statement around isolation guarantees (i.e., do you commit to no co-tenants on Dedicated pools, or is it "soft")?

—Karen
Karen Lee
CTO | TrueNorth Health

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
To: Karen Lee <karen.lee@truenorthhealth.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Mark Davis <mark.davis@truenorthhealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 23 Jun 2026 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: tenancy/SLAs & noisy-neighbor concerns — next steps

Hi Karen / Mark —

Thanks — confirmed for Wed 23 Jun 13:30 PT. Agenda for the POC (60–75m): 
1) Quick intros & goals (5m)
2) Provide the masked workload and traffic generator (we'll walk through your representative trace) (10m)
3) Run two short passes: Hosted API run (baseline) then Dedicated pool run with isolation config and KV-prefetch enabled (hands-on) (30m)
4) Compare tail latency percentiles + token cost, examine GPU utilization and preemption counters (15m)
5) Next steps and remediation plan (15m)

Preliminary answers to Karen's questions: 
- Hosted API: shared multi-tenant runtime; we optimize heavily for fairness and cost but cannot provide tenant-exclusion guarantees — latency isolation is "soft". Good for low-SLA, faster time-to-value.
- Dedicated capacity: reserved GPU pools for your account. By default we schedule only your workloads on the reserved nodes for the duration of the reservation — this gives strong practical isolation for noisy-neighbor risk (we do allow intra-customer shard consolidation but no third-party tenants).
- Private VPC / on-prem: full isolation under your control, includes customer-managed networking and KMS integration; best for highest regulatory/latency guarantees but requires more integration work.

I'm attaching our "redwood-isolation-playbook.pdf" which lists the knobs we use (node pinning, kernel selection, per-tenant throttles, continuous batching thresholds) and a short SLA-diff spreadsheet summarizing measurable SLOs and operational controls between tiers.

For the POC: please bring a masked sample trace representative of the morning spike. Aditya — on the call we'll enable dedicated pool with strict CPU/GPU reservation profile and enable per-request prefetch + KV cache.

If we find Dedicated still shows tail anomalies under your exact spike shape, we've had success with a hybrid: Dedicated baseline + short-lived private workers for critical windows (burst capacity) — we'll discuss feasibility.

Regards,
Monica
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.ai
